newsitem.title: FRANCE: French judge leaves Le Pen TV remarks uncut.
newsitem.headline: French judge leaves Le Pen TV remarks uncut.

text.p: A French judge on Thursday rejected a plea by far-right leader Jean Marie Le Pen that excepts from his speeches be deleted from a television documentary about his National Front party to be broadcast later in the day.

Le Pen had argued that the film violated the law by improperly using public statements he has made since since 1984. He insisted his remarks were his private "literary property" which could not be used without his permission.
Taking excerpts from public statements "must conform with the rules governing the protection of literary property", the anti-immigration campaigner told the newspaper France-Soir.
"You could no more quote from a compilation of speeches made over the past 20 years...than you could use a novel under the pretext that its author had just written an article," he said.

Le Pen acknowledged he had not seen the documentary, to be aired on France 2 public television on Thursday evening. He said he had asked the court to act on the basis of statements in advance by the show's hosts.
The documentary producers say the film analyses Le Pen's rise to political prominence and alleged inconsistencies in his statements about personal history and wealth.
